previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, diastolic heart failure, alcoholic cirrhosis, and prior right knee infection was admitted for revision total knee replacement. The surgery was performed successfully after removal of an antibiotic spacer. Postoperatively, she received two packed red blood cell transfusions for acute blood loss anemia and was managed with IV antibiotics, pain control, and DVT prophylaxis with Lovenox. Her wound healed well with no signs of infection, and labs showed improvement in hemoglobin. She was transitioned to oral medications, participated in physical therapy, and was discharged to a rehabilitation facility with instructions for anticoagulation, wound care, and follow-up. No active infection was found in intraoperative cultures.

Brief Hospital Course:
1. Hypotension:  On admission, the idea that the patient had 
evidence of sepsis given leukocytosis was considered.  Possible 
sources included septic knee (with resulting bacteremia); less 
evidence for pulmonary, GI, or GU.  Thought that hypovolemic, 
cardiogenic, anaphylactic etiologies less likely.  PE a 
possibility given ortho procedure this fall and prior clot 
history but seems less likely as not hypoxic.  No evidence for 
tamponade.  The patient was volume resuscitated, given empiric 
vancomycin and ceftriaxone to cover for possible septic joint, 
however knee films and ortho eval of right knee suggestive that 
knee not nidus of infection.  Held home ___ and beta blocker.  
Cardiac enzymes cycled.  

2. Acute on chronic renal failure:  Likely seccondary to 
hypotension.  Improved with fluids.  Renally dosed meds and 
avoid nephrotoxins, hold ___

3. Anemia:  Patient likely hemoconcentrated at admission. No 
active bleeding. Iron, B12, folate levels within normal limits 
___.  Followed hct daily, type +screen.  Patient did not 
require a transfusion.

4. Chronic pain:  Continued home pain medications with holding 
parameters

5. h/o chronic pancreatitis:  Continued pancreatic enzyme 
replacement, pain meds as above

6. DM: Continued insulin, follow fingersticks goal <150

7. CAD:  Continued ASA, statin. Held ___ in setting of renal 
failure and BB in setting of hypotension.

8. Crohn's disease: Continued mesalamine

9. CHF, chronic, diastolic: Held ___ and BB as above. Appeared 
euvolemic on exam.

10. h/o EtoH abuse: Patient denied any recent drinking.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted with hypotension (low blood pressure) and were 
treated with pressors and fluids with resolution of your 
symptoms. You were also given a short course of antibiotics. You 
were monitored after the discontinuation of your antibiotics and 
have done well. It is very important that you follow up with 
your primary care physician for further monitoring. You should 
also return to the ED if you develop a fever, night sweats, 
shortness of breath or any symptoms that concern you. You should 
also monitor your knee for any evidence of increased redness, 
swelling or increased drainage from your wound. 
.
Because you had decreased blood pressure your valsartan to 40 mg 
daily. Your metoprolol has been changed to metoprolol tartrate 
50mg twice daily. (Please ensure that your are taking metoprolol 
TARTRATE 50mg twice daily and not metoprolol SUCCINATE - you 
have had multiple prescriptions in the past by both names) You 
should discuss these changes with your regular doctor.

Please return to the ED or call your regular doctor if you 
experience fever, chills, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, 
knee pain that is worse, discharge or puss form your knee or any 
other symptom that concerns you.

HISTORY:  ___ female with hypotension, to assess for a cardiopulmonary
process.

TECHNIQUE:  Single portable AP radiograph of the chest was performed. 
Comparison is made with radiograph of ___.

FINDINGS:

The lungs are of low volume, most likely due to poor inspiratory effort.  The
cardiomediastinal silhouette is stable.  There is no focal pulmonary
consolidation.

CONCLUSION:

No acute cardiopulmonary process.

HISTORY:  ___ female with right IJ placed for hypotension.  Evaluate
line placement.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph one hour prior.

SINGLE PORTABLE UPRIGHT VIEW OF THE CHEST:  The right internal jugular line is
in place, and terminates near the cavoatrial junction.  There is no evidence
of pneumothorax.  Lung volumes remain low.  There is no focal consolidation. 
Heart size is inadequately assessed on AP radiograph.  Osseous structures are
unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  Satisfactory right internal jugular line placement, with no
evidence of pneumothorax.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with hypertension and new renal failure. Please
evaluate intra-abdominal process.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast axial images of the abdomen were obtained with
multiplanar reformatted images.

CT ABDOMEN WITHOUT CONTRAST:  Lung windows reveal hypoventilatory changes
bilaterally.  Atherosclerotic coronary artery calcifications are partially
visualized.  There is no evidence for pericardial or pleural effusion.

Evaluation of abdominal organs is limited by non-contrast technique.  Allowing
for this, the liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas, and adrenal glands appear
unremarkable.  Non-contrast evaluation of the kidneys is unremarkable and
there is no evidence of hydronephrosis or hydroureter.  Atherosclerotic
calcifications of the abdominal aorta and its branches are noted, though the
abdominal aorta is of normal caliber.  Scattered small mesenteric and
retroperitoneal lymph nodes are identified, none of which appear to meet CT
criteria for pathologic enlargement.  Intra-abdominal loops of large and small
bowel are of normal caliber.  A mild amount of pericolonic inflammatory
stranding appears new around the colonic flexure. There is no free air or free
fluid.

CT PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST:  The rectum and sigmoid colon are unremarkable.  A
Foley catheter is present within a moderately decompressed bladder which
contains non-dependent air within.  The adnexa appear unremarkable. Prominent
lymph nodes in the left hemipelvis extend into the inguinal region, measuring
up to 9 mm which does not meet CT criteria for pathologic enlargement and not
significantly changed compared to ___.

Bone windows reveal no worrisome lytic or sclerotic lesions.

IMPRESSION: Mild pericolonic stranding around the hepatic flexure is
nonspecific and the differential is broad, including inflammatory and other
acute colonic processes.

HISTORY:  Right total knee replacement revision, evaluate effusion.

AP, LATERAL, AND OBLIQUE RADIOGRAPHS OF THE RIGHT KNEE

FINDINGS:  Comparison is made to radiograph from ___.  Patient
is status post constrained prosthetic revision of the right knee total
arthroplasty.  The proximal portion of the long stem femoral component is not
visualized.  The visualized aspect does not demonstrate any lucency to suggest
hardware loosening.  There is no lucency around the cemented tibial component
to suggest loosening.  A knee joint effusion is present.  Skin staples have
been removed in the interval.

IMPRESSION:  Little interval change in patient status post constrained
prosthetic right total knee replacement.

HISTORY:  Left lower lobe crackles suggestive of pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the earlier study of this date, there is again
no evidence of acute pneumonia.  Right IJ catheter remains in place.

INDICATION:  Query DVT.

COMPARISON:  ___.

BILATERAL LOWER EXTREMITY VENOUS ULTRASOUND:  Grayscale and color and power
Doppler sonographic images were obtained that demonstrate wall-to-wall flow
with normal response to respiration and augmentation in the bilateral common
femoral, superficial femoral, popliteal veins with normal compressibility.
Bilateral calf veins were demonstrated.

IMPRESSION:  No DVT in the lower extremities.

HISTORY:  Evaluate for fracture.

AP, LATERAL AND MORTISE VIEWS OF THE RIGHT ANKLE

FINDINGS:  Comparison is made to the radiograph of ___ and there
is unchanged diffuse demineralization.  There is mild bimalleolar soft tissue
swelling.  There is a reticular appearance to the soft tissue surrounding the
ankle and lower calf that may represent soft tissue edema.  No fracture is
seen.  No dislocation is present.  The demineralized appearance of bone,
however, limits sensitivity for detection of subtle fractures.  No sclerotic,
lytic or erosive changes are present.  The ankle mortise is congruent.  There
is incidental note made of a plantar calcaneal enthesophyte.

IMPRESSION:  No fracture or dislocation.  Diffusely demineralized bones.
Bimalleolar soft tissue swelling.
